source.title: Simplicity Bias in Transformers and their Ability to Learn Sparse Boolean Functions
source.authors: S. Bhattamishra; Arkil Patel; Varun Kanade; P. Blunsom

record.tranche_reason: Tests random-label fitting and noisy-label learning on text and synthetic Boolean data using Transformers and LSTMs, extending the claim to sequence models and non-image tasks.
record.gate_note: The random-label experiment reports training fit and relative training time, but does not report test error on the randomly labeled SST data. Results cited from other work were excluded. Values shown only in plots are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures random-label fitting and training duration in sequence models, and learning under label noise on synthetic Boolean tasks. It extends the original settings to text and Boolean sequences.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's summary is broadly accurate but incomplete. Both architectures fit randomized SST labels near-perfectly with substantially longer training than true labels. Transformers often recover sparse Boolean targets despite noisy labels, whereas LSTMs overfit in the reported difficult settings. Some Transformers subsequently memorize noise, and Transformer robustness depends on task, sample size, depth, and training duration.
record.recipe_differences: Uses text SST and synthetic sparse Boolean tasks with Transformer and LSTM sequence models, rather than image classifiers and random image labels.
record.method_sensitivity: On sparse Boolean tasks, noise rate affects the training condition; Transformers may overfit after extended training. The authors also report sensitivity to hyperparameters and task/input setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Sensitivity increases during training on random Boolean labels and sentiment data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sequence models initially learn functions of lower sensitivity before learning more sensitive functions.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing dropout and L2 regularization on sparse parity slows LSTM convergence; sufficiently strong regularization prevents training fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit regularization changes optimization and fitting on structured sparse-parity tasks.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The random-label SST results provide no test accuracy and no exact timing comparison. The authors note that most results use artificial datasets and that empirical outcomes may depend on hyperparameters and experimental setup.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 23 contains training curves, but no separately described numeric values for individual rates or checkpoints; no figure values were estimated. Other results on Boolean functions do not measure the claim versions and were omitted.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error on independently randomized labels and a controlled demonstration that architecture and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.
The numerical slowdown factor and convergence time as a function of corruption fraction. Significantly more epochs alone does not resolve the small-constant-factor assertion.
All named input corruptions: shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
A full corruption sweep through 100%, with a steady test-error trajectory toward chance. Validation labels in the Boolean experiments remain clean.
Random-label fitting under the named regularizers and true-label generalization after removing them. Regularization experiments on sparse parity do not establish these comparisons.
Separate clean-example and noisy-example learning curves across models; the direct temporal evidence is limited to some Transformer runs.

missing.what: Random-label Boolean fitting: length-40 inputs, 1,000 training examples, and Transformers and LSTMs trained to zero training error. This directly bears on V1 despite the record dismissing other Boolean results as irrelevant.
A separate temporal row for signal learning followed by noise memorization in some Transformer runs after extended training.

Additional noisy-label conditions: sparse majority and dictator tasks at 10%–30% noise, and ten JUNTAS-(50,5) datasets at 10% noise. LSTMs reach 100% training accuracy despite poor validation performance in the reported difficult settings; Transformers generalize near-perfectly. These relevant conditions were incorrectly dismissed by the blanket Boolean-results exclusion.

record.verdict_notes: No V2 verdict is warranted from an unquantified slowdown. V6 has direct temporal evidence beyond sensitivity proxies. V4 predicts worsening test performance as corruption increases, not steadily improving generalization as the record's challenge rationale states. None of the supplied original sources is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The SST random-label experiment reports near-perfect training fit, but does not report test error at chance or pair the random-label result with generalization on the same models trained on true labels.
Reports only that random-label training takes significantly more iterations/epochs than true-label training; no constant-factor comparison or trend by fraction of corrupted labels.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
No sweep from zero to 100% corrupted labels or steady test-error trajectory. Noise experiments are on sparse Boolean tasks and report only selected noise rates.
No experiment tests whether weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation fail to prevent random-label fitting while their removal preserves true-label generalization.
No experiment tracks whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

rows.subject: Transformers
rows.operation_detail: Trained on SST with randomly assigned labels; authors report training accuracy and compare training duration with true labels.
rows.measure: Training accuracy and relative training duration
rows.baseline: Training on original dataset with true labels takes a few epochs
rows.value: Both models fit the training set near-perfectly; random-label training takes significantly more iterations/epochs.
rows.note: The text does not give test accuracy for random labels or exact duration values.
rows.check: Near-perfect random-label training fit establishes the measured V1 component. Split training accuracy from duration: the duration result cannot establish whether the slowdown exceeds a small constant factor. Random-label test accuracy and unchanged training hyperparameters are not established.

source_check.correct: V1: observed near-perfect random-label training fit. V2: cannot_determine; significantly longer training is reported without a numerical slowdown factor or corruption-fraction comparison. Split the measures.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix F, Figure 23 and accompanying paragraph; lines 2846–2882.
source_check.problem: The shared observed state overstates what the duration result establishes for V2.

rows.subject: Transformers
rows.operation_detail: Trained on sparse parity with randomly flipped training labels.
rows.value: Perfect generalization accuracy; training accuracy converges at 1 − η. In some cases, after many iterations post-convergence, Transformers begin to overfit on the noise.
rows.note: Training accuracy is reported as 1 − η, rather than perfect, and the text notes later overfitting in some cases.
rows.check: For V4, training initially plateaus at 1 − η rather than fitting perfectly, while clean validation accuracy is perfect. Separate the later-training observation: some runs begin fitting noise only after learning the signal, directly bearing on V6. Figure 6 specifically shows 10% noise; the prose covers 5%–20%.

source_check.correct: V4: partial, with perfect clean generalization and training accuracy converging at 1 − η. V6: observed in some runs, with noise overfitting beginning after many additional post-convergence iterations. Separate the temporal result.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, Robustness to noise, lines 1034–1071; Figure 6.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state fits V4 but understates the reported V6 sequence in the specified runs.

rows.subject: LSTMs
rows.operation_detail: Trained on sparse parity with noisy training labels; authors state they overfit.
rows.value: LSTMs overfit on the training data while achieving chance-level validation accuracy.
rows.note: The text says recurrent-model behavior is the same as with clean data; no exact training accuracy for this noisy setting is stated.
rows.check: Reversed is unjustified: overfitting and chance validation accuracy also occur with clean labels, so this does not demonstrate a reversed noise-response trajectory. The noisy-setting prose does not separately quantify training accuracy. Remove the unexplained numbers_found value.
